regions.name: east-farmstead
regions.brief: Solve the farmstead west of the branching market lane as one irregular group. Own the long dark timber barn at root ground foot approximately (714,320), sheep and their small farm enclosure around (753,298), the warm timber gable shed (764,353), the ivory canvas-roofed structure (804,328), larger tile-roofed plaster/timber house (838,358), blue-roofed windmill house (808,390), and long dark-thatch barn (834,425). Match roof ridge orientations, footprint proportions, overlaps and open lawn between them. The blue mill's framed white body, vivid blue two-slope roof, front timber hub and four substantial sails are distinctive. Complete it with attached axle, real wooden sail members, full rear roof and back walls. Complete the clipped upper barn behind the crop boundary. Sheep must have bodies, heads and legs; roofs must have gable ends, eaves thickness and ridge structure. All associated small goods, carts and fences in this farm group are yours. Exclude the market structures east of root x865, roads, roadside lamps, and all natural features. This is a building group and a complex mill: use your own solve loop; descend again only if inspection establishes a real internal subproblem.

regions.name: east-market
regions.brief: Solve the village market court in the wedge between the two roads. Own the low orange/tan irregular roofed market building with open supported porch at approximate root foot (887,455); circular blue-grey masonry well with dark blue pitched canopy at (925,397); light cloth awning stall around (884,413); covered wooden stalls around (881,371) and (961,435); pale stacked rectangular goods/canvas display near (921,437); barrels/crates/benches around the court and uphill lane, including the stacks near (925,367), (975,429), and the few tiny people. Verify these approximate feet from your target before building. The reference depicts separate well, stalls, goods, people and low shop with open ground between; do not collapse this into one building or line up stalls uniformly. Build complete backs, thick roof planes, full round well masonry with an actual opening and inside wall, attached beams and standing goods. The green pin obscures part of the northeast corner: complete hidden court plausibly but do not model the pin. Pale farmhouse and pondside goods visible at the far right belong to east-lakeside. The farmstead buildings at the left edge belong to east-farmstead. Exclude all roadside lamps, through-roads and natural features.

regions.name: east-lakeside
regions.brief: Solve the three distinct lakeside homes and their small pondside utility props. Own the small dark-thatch cottage on the lower left at approximate root foot (981,518); larger two-story blue-slate timber/plaster house (1068,488), with its chimney, deep roof and attached low timber porch/storage platform; pale-thatch timber/plaster house north of the road (1102,441), including its chimney and side attachment. Also own the small canvas shelter beside trees near (1110,378), low covered goods/cart near (1014,402), dark upright item (1028,404), and barrel/crate stack (1046,401) on the pond's lower bank. Check all ground feet by eye in the crop; source anchors are approximate. Keep three house footprints, heights, roof materials, orientation and large garden gaps distinct. Preserve attachment to the fork and winding lower lane without duplicating those roads. Complete full wall boxes with timber framing, visible and back doors/windows, thick two-slope roofs and gable end walls; place foundations at ground. Roofs must not be pyramids. The green map pin and central market visible at the left edge are context, not yours. Exclude all lamps, roads and natural features, including the pond and trees.

regions.name: east-windmills
regions.brief: Solve both freestanding timber windmills at the eastern boundary as a related pair. Approximate root ground feet are (1178,388) for the smaller western mill and (1242,370) for the taller eastern mill. Both have stout grey stone polygonal bases, tapered timber/plaster tower bodies with diagonal bracing, orange-brown projecting timber belts, small warm roof caps, and four dark grey slatted lattice sails attached by timber arms to a forward hub. Match the different heights, spacing, body taper, stone base footprint, sail angles and front-facing plane orientation. The rotor crosses are diagonally oriented in the reference. These are intricate volumetric assemblies, not crossed flat rectangles: build wood rails, cross slats, hubs/axles, wall/base thickness, and full back structure. Inspect the tower in four compass views and ensure rotor does not intersect roof or tower. The edge behind them is the finite diorama boundary; do not extend land or build the distant graphic background. Trees, road and lamps visible in the crop are context owned elsewhere. Own only the two mills and immediate structural bases/steps.
